correctness.rationale: The graph and all 495 four-vertex induced subgraphs are explicitly constructed; two exhaustive face predicates agree on all 4096 subsets. Two full Hasse-acyclic Morse matchings are certified. The first reduces to six degree-six and 21 degree-seven cells, and exact signed unit elimination gives one primitive nonzero boundary column, implying the integral wedge of five six-dimensional and twenty seven-dimensional spheres. Direct mod-two simplex ranks 11,55,165,330,462,450,265 corroborate, but do not replace, the integral proof. Purity and lower-dimensional homology imply nonshellability.

originality.rationale: A complete integral homotopy computation for the ordinary four-cut complex of the canonical icosahedral graph is not implied by the inspected primary general theorems (their face-skeleton hypothesis fails) or by the publicly indexed three-cut result for the same graph. Exact object aliases and stronger-family searches did not return the same claim. This is evidence-limited originality, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: Semantic search indexes and open web queries do not exhaust all mathematics literature; an unindexed exact special-case computation may exist.
The indexed four-cut results on other graphs and high-girth families were checked at the summary level, so a surprisingly general uninspected theorem outside their described scope remains possible.
The classification is proved only for this finite graph and only in the ordinary cut-complex sense.

value.rationale: The icosahedral graph is the canonical regular five-valent Platonic skeleton. Its four-cut level is a natural topological invariant in an established cut-complex filtration but is not implied by the known three-cut calculation; the generic primary homology theorem fails its skeleton hypothesis. A complete integral homotopy classification, adjacent-degree ranks 5 and 20, non-shellability, and exact characterization of the twelve missing six-element simplices by closed vertex neighborhoods provide distinctive structural information without claiming a broader family.
